rounds.text: Radico Khaitan is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a 74% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 41% [E20, E21]. This profitability is backed by strong cash generation, featuring an operating cash flow of Rs 743 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 504 Cr in March 2026, alongside a healthy 1.23x cash conversion [E34, E35, E36]. The business efficiency far outpaces sector benchmarks, delivering a superior ROA of 14.15%, ROE of 18.23%, and ROCE of 22.49% [E8, E9, E10]. Management is successfully capturing market tailwinds through premiumisation, upgrading its Prestige and Above volume growth guidance to 30% for FY27 while reporting a record 10 million cases in Q1 FY27 [E74, E84]. Furthermore, the company's financial position is strengthening rapidly through debt reduction, with borrowings dropping to Rs 394 Cr in Sep 2026 and net debt reduced by Rs 138 crores since March 2026 [E39, E87]. Conceded: the stock trades at elevated valuation multiples, including a P/E of 71.5 and a price-to-book of 15.66x, alongside a low dividend yield of 0.21% [E1, E2, E4].

Radico Khaitan trades at an extraordinary valuation that is completely disconnected from fundamental reality, sporting a trailing P/E ratio of 71.5 and a P/B of 15.66x [E1, E2], which towers over sector benchmarks of 17.48x and 1.71x respectively [E6, E7]. This excessive pricing leaves virtually zero room for error, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 2,251 per share against a market price of Rs 4,290, resulting in a staggering margin of safety of -90.6% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the company's reverse DCF reveals that today's price already aggressively prices in 26.0% earnings growth—far higher than the 17.0% assumed in the base case [E47]—while historical performance shows the worst peak-to-trough drawdown on record hits an alarming -92.5% [E53]. Conceded: the company demonstrates robust operational metrics including a 14.15% ROA, 18.23% ROE, and 22.49% ROCE that comfortably exceed sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10], alongside healthy operating cash flows of Rs 743 Cr and free cash flows of Rs 504 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. Nevertheless, management itself concedes that the global environment has turned increasingly volatile with heightened uncertainty surrounding input costs and supply chains [E89], making the current price-led expansion [E56] an extremely precarious entry point for investors.

The bear warns of a rich P/E of 71.5 and a P/B of 15.66x [E1, E2], but these multiples are fully justified by elite returns on capital, including an ROE of 20.3% and ROCE of 24.2% [E13, E12] that dwarf sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value sits below the market price at Rs 2,251 [E45, E46], but static models miss the compounding power of a business growing quarterly sales at 16% [E17] and 3-year profit growth at 41% [E20]. While the historical drawdown of -92.5% is noted [E53], the company has fundamentally transformed its balance sheet, reducing net debt by Rs 138 crores since March 2026 [E87] and operating with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.11x [E37]. Finally, the bear's reliance on management's warnings about global volatility [E89] overlooks tangible mitigation: captive ENA production capacity of 33 crores liters comfortably covers total requirements of up to 30 crores liters [E85], securing supply chains against external shocks.

Conceded: the company operates with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.11x [E37] and has reduced net debt by Rs 138 crores since March 2026 [E87]. However, the bull's dismissal of valuation risks ignores the severe disconnect highlighted by the discounted cash flow model, which places intrinsic value at Rs 2,251 against a market price of Rs 4,290, resulting in a -90.6% margin of safety [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands a 26.0% earnings growth rate, surpassing the 17.0% base case assumption [E47]. While captive ENA production capacity of 33 crores liters covers requirements [E85], management explicitly acknowledges a global environment turning increasingly volatile with heightened uncertainty around input costs and supply chains [E89], leaving little room for error at a rich P/E of 71.5 [E1] and EV/EBITDA of 48.66x against a sector benchmark of 11.29x [E11]. Finally, the screen engine itself explicitly flags decelerating earnings growth and a DCF overvaluation of -91% as primary bear warnings [E66, E67].

Conceded: the DCF model calculates an intrinsic value of Rs 2,251 against the market price of Rs 4,290 [E45, E46], and the reverse DCF implies a 26.0% earnings growth rate [E47]. However, the market's willingness to price Radico Khaitan at a premium is fully backed by superior operational metrics that blow past sector benchmarks, including an ROA of 14.15% versus 4.85%, an ROE of 18.23% versus 8.45%, and an ROCE of 22.49% versus 9.33% [E8, E9, E10]. The bear highlights management's warning on global volatility [E89], but ignores that this volatility is actively mitigated by a massive captive ENA production capacity of 33 crores liters that easily outstrips total requirements of 28 to 30 crores liters [E85]. Furthermore, the bear's claim of decelerating earnings is directly contradicted by accelerating fundamental performance, such as a 74% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21], a 41% profit growth over 3 years [E20], and operating margins expanding by 7 percentage points in TTM and 4 percentage points in the Sep 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. Institutional money flow explicitly reads positive with domestic institutions increasing their holdings by 3.18 percentage points and foreign institutions adding 0.42 percentage points [E42, E43, E44], proving that sophisticated market participants recognize the underlying strength of the business. Finally, management has walked the talk on financial discipline by reducing term loans by Rs 75.7 Crore since March 2026 and lowering borrowings to Rs 394 Cr [E39, E86], cementing a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.11x [E37] that makes the balance sheet exceptionally robust.

Conceded: domestic and foreign institutions increased their holdings by 3.18 and 0.42 percentage points respectively [E42, E43], and TTM profit growth hit 74% [E21]. However, this backward-looking operational strength has blinded the market to a severe valuation disconnect, evidenced by a massive DCF overvaluation of -90.6% where intrinsic value sits at Rs 2,251 against a market price of Rs 4,290 [E45, E46]. The bull points to captive ENA capacity of 33 crores liters over requirements [E85] to dismiss management's warning on global volatility and supply chain challenges [E89, E90], yet ignores that management explicitly admitted to building up higher stock levels precisely to mitigate increasing grain prices [E82], proving that input cost pressures are real and active. Furthermore, while the bull celebrates the debt reduction and a clean 0.11x debt-to-equity ratio [E37, E39, E86], a pristine balance sheet does not insulate a stock trading at an astronomical P/E of 71.5x to 79.98x against a sector benchmark of 17.48x [E1, E6]. The reverse DCF reveals that today's price already demands a grueling 26.0% earnings growth rate just to justify itself, outstripping the base case of 17.0% [E47], while the rules-based screen explicitly flags decelerating earnings growth as a core bear risk [E66].

evidence.fact: The company expects its Prestige and Above portfolio to deliver over 25% volume growth during FY27.

evidence.fact: Management remains confident of sustaining an EBITDA margin of around 20% for FY27.
evidence.quote: With premium brands accounting for an increasing share of our business, we remain confident of sustaining EBITDA margin of around 20% for FY27 while continuing to invest behind our brands and strengthen our long-term competitive position.

evidence.fact: Management stated that premiumisation continues to define the Indian spirits industry, supported by rising aspirations, an evolving cocktail culture, and the expanding hospitality sector.
evidence.quote: Premiumisation continues to define the Indian spirits industry. Rising aspirations, an evolving cocktail culture and the expanding hospitality sector are steadily drawing consumers towards brands built on quality, heritage and authenticity.

evidence.fact: Management noted that Karnataka's rationalised duty framework and Tamil Nadu's signals are supporting the long-term formalisation of the industry.
evidence.quote: In Karnataka, the rationalised duty framework is showing early signs of a healthier, more premium-friendly market. Tamil Nadu, the country’s largest market, is also sending encouraging signals. Such progressive steps widen the opportunity for organised, branded players and support the long-term formalisation of the industry.
